answer: Cross-epoch trajectory matching. Each identity commits a rolling signed log of task selections, and a long horizon check compares that log to itself across epochs: divergence beyond a fixed distance flags the identity as cloned. Enforcement requires a stable vertex in behaviour space, so fresh clones cannot inherit an older identity’s trajectory without replaying it. Attacker cost: every clone must reproduce the full history sequence under its own key, paying compute and latency per identity, and any drift still reveals shared selection nectar patterns.
